title: Longest Ascent

story.briefing: Somewhere in the calibration log is the longest run of strictly rising readings — not necessarily consecutive, just in order. Its length sets the tolerance band.
story.success: Longest ascent measured. The tolerance band is set.

description: Given an array of readings, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence — a set of readings taken in their original order, each strictly greater than the one before, but not necessarily adjacent. An empty array returns 0.
hints: Comparing each reading against every earlier one gives the right answer but grows quadratically. The hidden tests are large enough that this will not finish.
Keep, for each possible ascent length, the smallest value that could end an ascent of that length. That list is always sorted, which is the opening you need.

Maintain a sorted list of ascent-ending values. For each reading, find the first entry that is not smaller and replace it; if none exists, append. The list length is the answer — its contents are not a real subsequence.
